Tasks: 5 SWE-bench Verified tasks. Configurations: 12 specifications (10 Spec Kit-template variants + raw + oracle) x 3 thinking efforts (low, high, max) x 15 repeats = 2,700 runs; analyses on 11 specs (oracle excluded). Baseline: full specification. Held constant: model (Kimi K3), scaffold (mini-swe-agent), temperature 1.0, Docker image, no network, turn and cost caps; spec content differs only by removed sections (not length-controlled). Acceptance tests: SWE-bench harness. Repetitions: 15 per cell. Human intervention: none; 112 runs capped at 60 turns re-run at 120

Bare user story vs full spec: cost +29.7%, turns +16.4% (credible at 90%, positive on all 5 tasks; 13%-115% by task); acceptance scenarios only single section with credible effect (+7.0% turns); other single sections -5.4% to -2.4% cost (n.s.). No variant credibly changes solve rate (all within 7.5 pts). Variance unaffected (x1.34). Spec matters more at low effort (ratio x2.13) than max (x1.61). Predictor: no probe 161% median error; 1 probe (0.11 USD) 36%; 10 probes 25%; r = 0.72 vs 0.08 without probe. Significance: at 95% two of three established effects include zero (posterior P>0 = 0.97-0.98)

Distinguished large cuts from full spec on cost/turns, not single sections, and not on solve rate (ceiling effect: 4 of 5 tasks >= 98%). Repeatable: 15 repeats per cell, prior sensitivity analysis; specs cannot be ranked (split-half Spearman 0.41, projected 0.58 at 15 repeats). Limitations stated: single model, five tasks, variants not length-controlled, predictor ignores task-specific prompt sensitivity, percentages depend on price schedule

Single model (Kimi K3) is a core limitation; sparse set of tasks; predictor omits task-specific prompt sensitivity; token/dollar split specific to price schedule and cache rate; specs constructed (LLM-drafted), not collected from engineers. Future: more tasks and models, real workflows with engineer-written specs
